parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized pure Node ESM, .mjs suffixes, zero npm dependencies, manual argparse behavior, black-box executable probing, /output delivery, split modules, and the core output of three matching documents.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed behavior itself, then launched six subagents, one per file: fields, query, qparser, index, argparse, and entry, while keeping integration and final verification with the parent.
parallel.implementation: The children produced /output/lib/*.mjs modules plus /output/test11.mjs under a parent-defined camelCase contract, including createIn, addDocument, addArgument, and parseArgs; argparse received the most detailed testing.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The AgentSwarm result returned all six child handoffs; the parent ran the entry script against the generated modules, read the final files, and delivered the /output artifact listed in status.
parallel.verification: Parallel verified executable behavior before delegation, then ran integrated Node checks for valid args, equals args, missing args, unknown extras, duplicate args, help output normalization, and empty or unicode values.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No child was left unfinished and no merge was visibly skipped, but the official evaluator still failed the final artifact at 48/70, likely due hidden behavioral or module API mismatches not exposed by local checks.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, manual parsing, /output, and output-count requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent handled probing, all module implementations, the entry script, verification, and final response without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote root-level modules argparser.mjs, fields.mjs, index.mjs, query.mjs, qparser.mjs, and test11.mjs using Python-style names such as add_argument, parse_args, create_in, and add_document.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial entry imported the root-level modules it had just written, generated an index directory manifest on commit, and delivered an artifact containing those six files.
serial.verification: Serial checked the executable and its own Node output for valid args, missing --c, --help, equals-form args, unknown args, positionals, and empty or whitespace values.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Serial also failed official evaluation at 49/70, with the visible likely defects limited to incomplete hidden argparse or Whoosh API fidelity rather than any coordination breakdown.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel acknowledged the full ESM, .mjs, manual parsing, no external dependency, black-box executable, and output placement requirements before delegating.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial acknowledged the same prompt and worked directly from the same executable observations and source requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was materially similar; the main difference was the parallel parent choosing a JavaScript-style library API contract while serial preserved more Python-style names.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the work into six non-overlapping child-owned files while the parent retained behavior discovery, integration, and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all discovery, implementation, integration, and verification in the single main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more actors but ownership was explicit; serial had no delegation and therefore no handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave all children a shared fixed inter-module contract, including exact file paths, imports, and exported symbols; the contract chose camelCase helper names under /output/lib.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial encoded interfaces locally with root-level files and Python-style names, avoiding inter-agent interface negotiation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The API-shape contrast is visible, but the parallel contract was not missing or inconsistent across agents; children implemented what the parent requested and the entry imported those names.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced class-based fields, query, qparser, index, argparse, and an entry that called new TEXT, createIn, addDocument, and parseArgs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced functions/classes closer to the Python surface, including TEXT(options), create_in, add_document, add_argument, parse_args, and a qparser with a basic includes matcher.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both final programs print 3 for valid inputs, but their support module APIs and internals differ; this is an ordinary implementation difference that may affect hidden module-level checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All six subagents completed and returned handoffs; the parent received the aggregate AgentSwarm result and then inspected the final files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; its writes and tests stayed within the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced result handoffs but did not visibly lose, ignore, or fail to join any completed child result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct file paths and the parent integrated them through imports from /output/lib, with no same-file conflict or overwrite visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all root-level files itself and integrated them through root-relative imports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both attempts used coherent internal imports; parallel's shared workspace did not produce a visible collision, while serial avoided shared-state risk by construction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed substantial black-box probing before delegation, child-level argparse checks, integrated Node checks, help comparison, duplicate-argument checks, and final file reads before declaring completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran black-box probes and integrated Node checks, including valid, missing, help, equals, unknown, positional, and empty-value cases, then declared completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was broader in visible edge coverage, but neither run had evaluator-complete acceptance before closure; both later failed the official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a larger budget, 476.386 agent seconds and 572153 tokens, but completed normally with no timeout and with all six subagents completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster, 132.431 agent seconds and 164156 tokens, with no timeout and no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was more expensive and slower, but the extra budget use did not visibly displace unfinished work or produce a timeout-based coordination failure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both solutions failed, with parallel at 48/70 and serial at 49/70. The visible process difference is that parallel delegated six files after defining a camelCase /output/lib contract, while serial wrote root-level modules with Python-style API names. Both attempts produced runnable entry scripts and both ran representative checks, so the one-sample score gap is best treated as an ordinary implementation or hidden-evaluator coverage difference rather than a proven parallel coordination failure.
parallel_contributors: Parent-defined camelCase support-module contract under /output/lib, later used consistently by the entry script.
Broader visible argparse edge probing and integrated checks, followed by final reads of all generated files.
serial_contributors: Single actor preserved Python-style helper names in root-level modules.
Integrated checks covered valid, missing, help, equals-form, unknown, positional, and empty or whitespace values.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel exported and used createIn/addDocument/addArgument/parseArgs, while serial exported and used create_in/add_document/add_argument/parse_args.
Parallel modeled TEXT and ID as classes requiring new; serial modeled TEXT and ID as callable functions.
Serial persisted a segments.json manifest on commit; parallel kept the index entirely in memory.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official counts are available in the mounted pair, so the exact hidden testcase responsible for the 48/70 versus 49/70 gap cannot be identified from accessible evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; implementation differences are observed but not proven concurrency-caused

The parent explicitly retained integration responsibility after the swarm and ran the combined entry script against the generated modules.
The required entry file was assigned to a child and then included in the final artifact; no unowned final packaging step is visible.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from probing to delegation, integration checks, final reads, and completion response.
The parent performed serial executable probes before delegation, but the gate did not leave implementation unfinished or visibly shorten closure.
Investigation was followed by successful module production, integration, and verification; no deadline-constrained incomplete later phase is visible.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was starved; the parent integrated all child outputs and tests completed.
The six-child fan-out consumed more tokens and time than serial, but the run did not exhaust the cell budget or drop required work before closure.
No child received an overbroad unfinished assignment; each child completed a bounded single-file scope and returned a result.

Child briefs included the original program, hard ESM/no-dependency rules, paths, exports, and acceptance expectations; any API naming weakness came from the chosen implementation contract, not an omitted known requirement.
The parallel parent supplied an explicit inter-module contract and the child outputs interoperated with the entry script during integrated checks.
No known finding or file state disappeared in transfer; child handoffs reported file paths and exports and were then inspected by the parent.
The aggregate swarm result was large but the parent consumed it, ran integrated tests, and read final files, so no material nonconsumption is shown.
No child or parent acted on a superseded workspace, requirement, dependency, or decision state after newer state was visible.
Returned child reports did not present incompatible contracts that remained unadjudicated; the parent used one consistent contract.
The parent did declare completion, but it first ran integrated checks and no parent-visible unresolved acceptance mismatch is evident before closure.
There was no replacement or retry agent that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints or current workspace state.

candidates.reason: No executed child was explicitly stopped, cancelled, or interrupted before its needed work or result was finalized.

The parent ran integrated verification after receiving and using the swarm outputs, not before a later merge.
Completed delegated implementations were retrievable and were joined into the final file tree that the parent tested and read.
No verifier child produced a trapped finding; verification was performed by the argparse child and parent with visible returned results.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; every child in the swarm reported completed status.
The completed swarm result was available and the parent proceeded consistently with it by running tests and reading generated files.
There is no timeout or near-deadline waiting episode; the parent resumed after the swarm result and continued active verification.
Different children wrote different files with a common contract, and no competing design over the same behavior required reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source file; the only edit to test11.mjs was by the same child that created it.
No agent replaced a non-entry source file produced or actively owned by another agent.
The entry deliverable was written and then edited by the same owning child, not overwritten by a separate live actor.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another actor's final-tree work.
Although children wrote into a shared /output workspace, file ownership was isolated and no unstable state or provenance problem is shown.
No generated temporary file, cache, tool, process, or auxiliary artifact from one actor was consumed by another as reference input.
